m1_zero_omission_notes.chapter_executive_summary: Explores tangents to a circle, proving that the tangent at any point is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact, and that tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length.

detailed_section_hierarchy.section_number_title: 10.1 Tangent to a Circle & Radius Perpendicularity
detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point. Theorem 10.1: The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

margin_boxes_and_in_text_notes.full_content: OP ⊥ XY at point of contact P.

detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: Theorem 10.2: The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal (PQ = PR).

margin_boxes_and_in_text_notes.full_content: Tangents PQ and PR from external P are equal (PQ = PR).

glossary_and_key_terms.definition: A line that intersects a circle at exactly one point.
glossary_and_key_terms.contextual_example_or_usage: Line AB touching circle at P

glossary_and_key_terms.definition: The common point of the tangent line and the circle.

formulas_rules_and_laws.name: Tangent Length Property
formulas_rules_and_laws.statement_or_expression: PQ = PR (Tangents from external point P)
formulas_rules_and_laws.variable_definitions: P = external point, Q, R = points of contact
formulas_rules_and_laws.model_application_example: If PQ = 8 cm, then PR = 8 cm.

m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.objective_or_aim: Prove PQ = PR for external point P.
step_by_step_procedure: ΔOQP ≅ ΔORP by RHS => PQ = PR by CPCT.
m3_practical_activities_lab_and_step_by_.scientific_or_logical_conclusion: Lengths of tangents from external point are equal.

level_2_short_answer_questions_2_to_3_ma.question: Prove that in two concentric circles, chord of larger circle touching smaller circle is bisected at point of contact.
level_2_short_answer_questions_2_to_3_ma.model_answer: Let AB be chord of C1 touching C2 at P. OP ⊥ AB (Radius ⊥ Tangent). Perpendicular from center to chord bisects the chord => AP = PB.

level_3_long_answer_and_reasoning_5_mark.question: Prove that the parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
level_3_long_answer_and_reasoning_5_mark.model_answer: Let ABCD circumscribe circle touching at P,Q,R,S. AB+CD = AD+BC (Equal tangent sums). Since ABCD is parallelogram, AB=CD and AD=BC => 2AB = 2AD => AB = AD. Adjacent sides equal => ABCD is a rhombus.

level_4_competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: A triangle ABC is drawn to circumscribe a circle of radius 4 cm such that segments BD and DC are 8 cm and 6 cm.

questions_and_answers.question: Find sides AB and AC.
questions_and_answers.answer: Using equal tangents and area formula (Heron's = sum of 3 inner triangles): AB = 15 cm, AC = 13 cm.

m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.frequent_student_error: Assuming secant and tangent are the same.
m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.root_cause: Failing to distinguish 1 point of contact vs 2 intersection points.
m7_common_pitfalls_and_misconceptions.correct_approach: Secant intersects at 2 points; Tangent touches at exactly 1 point.
